ip_top_stories.title: Book Publishers Sue Google Over AI Training, Escalating a Legal Standoff
ip_top_stories.summary: Major publishers including Hachette, Cengage, and Elsevier have filed a copyright infringement lawsuit against Google, alleging the company used millions of copyrighted books without authorisation to train its Gemini AI models. The case marks a significant escalation in legal battles between publishers and AI developers over training data. Author Scott Turow is also among the plaintiffs.

ip_top_stories.title: Mandatory AI standards to hit parliament next year, PM warns against copyright 'theft'
ip_top_stories.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese announced mandatory AI standards legislation to be introduced to parliament next year, and explicitly warned against what he characterised as copyright theft by AI companies. The announcement includes plans to strengthen copyright protections for Australian creators and the establishment of a new Office of AI.

ip_top_stories.title: EU study backs copyright registry pilot for AI training opt-outs
ip_top_stories.summary: A European Union study has endorsed a pilot copyright registry that would allow rights holders to opt out of having their works used for AI training. The proposal is intended to provide a practical mechanism for creators to assert their rights under the EU AI Act's copyright transparency requirements.

ip_top_stories.title: AI firms' mass purchase and destruction of books for model training fuels copyright debate
ip_top_stories.summary: Reports have emerged that AI companies are purchasing large quantities of physical books and destroying them after digitisation for use in model training, a practice that is intensifying debate around copyright and fair use. Critics argue the practice exploits a legal grey area while undermining the economic interests of authors and publishers.

ip_top_stories.title: Why a fight over 61,000 recordings could shape the future of AI music licensing
ip_top_stories.summary: A legal dispute involving 61,000 music recordings is being closely watched as a potential precedent-setter for how AI companies must license creative works for training purposes. The outcome could establish key principles around whether existing licensing frameworks apply to AI training datasets.

ip_further_links.title: Kenyan Author Loses Copyright Claim Over AI-Generated Works in Landmark Ruling
ip_further_links.summary: A Kenyan court has rejected a copyright claim over AI-generated works in a ruling that may have broad implications for how authorship and originality are assessed in AI-assisted creation.

ip_further_links.title: Australia's AI Ambitions Hinge on 1968 Copyright Law
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of how Australia's decades-old Copyright Act is becoming a central battleground as the government attempts to craft AI policy, with calls for reform to address gaps exposed by generative AI.

ip_further_links.title: Rod Sims: Governments must not give AI companies a free pass on copyright
ip_further_links.summary: Former ACCC chair Rod Sims argues that governments should resist pressure from AI companies to weaken copyright protections and must ensure creators are fairly compensated for use of their works in AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Ed Husic says weakening copyright to benefit AI companies would betray Labor party's ethos
ip_further_links.summary: Australian Labor MP Ed Husic has publicly opposed any move to weaken copyright protections for the benefit of AI companies, framing it as contrary to Labor's values of supporting workers and creators.

ip_further_links.title: Courts won't settle the fight over AI and creative work: Politics will - Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis arguing that the fundamental questions around AI and copyright are ultimately political rather than legal, and that legislative action will be required to resolve tensions that courts cannot fully address.

ip_further_links.title: The Script singer accuses AI companies of copyright theft 'on an industrial scale'
ip_further_links.summary: Danny O'Donoghue of The Script has publicly accused AI companies of committing copyright theft on an industrial scale by using musicians' recordings without consent or compensation for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: OpenAI's Copyright Lawsuit Crisis Reveals the Hidden Cost of Safer AI
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis of how the accumulation of copyright lawsuits against OpenAI is creating financial and reputational pressure that may influence the company's approach to training data sourcing and safety investments.

ip_further_links.title: Display Maker Says AI-Made Images Don't Infringe Rival's IP
ip_further_links.summary: A display technology company has argued in a legal filing that AI-generated images used in its products do not infringe a competitor's intellectual property rights, in a case that tests the boundaries of AI output and IP ownership.

ip_further_links.title: [Guest Post] Humans, not muses — IPKat
ip_further_links.summary: An IPKat guest post examining the philosophical and legal implications of treating human creators as mere inspiration sources for AI systems, with discussion of how authorship doctrine should respond.

ip_further_links.title: There's a solution to AI paying for copyright that no one's talking about
ip_further_links.summary: Opinion piece proposing a lesser-discussed licensing mechanism that could enable AI companies to compensate rights holders at scale, bypassing the current deadlock between litigation and voluntary deals.
